cases.title: Middle East Red Balloon 2024
cases.summary: The All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office received a report from a U.S. military Service consisting of one minute and thirty-six seconds of full-motion video footage captured by a camera aboard a U.S. military platform in the Middle East in 2024. According to the reporting Service, the recording likely depicts a slow-moving spheroidal object. AARO assesses, with high confidence, that the object depicted in the video is almost certainly (≥95% likelihood) a consumer-grade reflective foil balloon. AARO bases its assessment on the object's strong morphological consistency with other resolved imagery depicting balloons and its behavioral correlation with recorded wind speed and direction during the event.

cases.summary: In October 2017, an infrared sensor onboard a force protection aerostat near Al Taqaddum Air Base, Iraq, captured 17 minutes of video of an unidentified object. AARO used geo-locational data from the aerostat to assess the object's speed and direction of travel.

cases.title: Western U.S. Objects

cases.title: South Asian Object 1
cases.summary: In an open hearing on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena before the Senate Armed Services Committee on April 19, Dr. Sean Kirkpatrick, director of the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO), shared a video depicting an unidentified object with an apparent atmospheric wake or cavitation trailing it as it moves across the sensor’s field of view from left to right. An MQ-9 forward-looking infrared video sensor captured this footage in South Asia as it was recording another MQ-9. After analysis of the full motion video, inclusion of additional footage with a longer focal length, and analysis of commercial flight data in the region, AARO assesses that the object likely is a commercial aircraft and that the trailing cavitation is a sensor artifact resultant of video compression. Case resolution is pending final review.

cases.title: Mt. Etna Object
cases.summary: In December 2018, a forward-looking infrared video sensor aboard an uncrewed U.S. Air Force platform captured this footage while operating over the Mediterranean Sea. This footage depicts an object that appears to be transiting a plume of superheated gas and ash produced by an eruption of Mt. Etna, a volcano in Sicily, Italy. AARO coordinated an interagency and international analytical effort that determined that optical effects from the intense atmospheric conditions near the volcano distorted the video, causing the object to appear to transit the plume. AARO assesses with moderate confidence that the footage instead depicts a balloon approximately 170 kilometers from the caldera traveling at wind speed and direction.

cases.title: Puerto Rico Objects
cases.summary: On April 26, 2013, an infrared sensor onboard a U.S. Customs and Border Protection aircraft captured footage of a UAP event over the Rafael Hernandez Airport near Aguadilla, Puerto Rico. The footage appears to depict a UAP moving at high speed, splitting into two objects, and entering and exiting the water before disappearing into the ocean off Puerto Rico's northwestern coast. AARO assesses with high confidence that the objects did not demonstrate anomalous speeds or flight behaviors. An Intelligence Community partner's reconstruction of the flight path and look angle from the infrared sensor indicates that the video instead depicts two objects traveling near each other rather than a single object splitting into two. This reconstruction also demonstrates that the objects traveled in a straight line at wind speed and did not enter the water at any point.

files.title: 2013 Puerto Rico Object Reconstruction
files.description: This video shows a Systems Toolkit digital reconstruction of "The Puerto Rico Object" unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) event as seen from above. The reconstruction shows the aircraft's flight path, an onboard infrared sensor’s look angle to the ground, and the objects’ assessed flight path. This reconstruction demonstrates that the objects traveled in a straight line at wind speed over land. On April 26, 2013, an infrared sensor onboard a U.S. Customs and Border Protection aircraft captured footage of a UAP event over the Rafael Hernandez Airport near Aguadilla, Puerto Rico. AARO assesses with high confidence that the objects did not demonstrate anomalous speeds or flight behaviors.

files.title: Al Taqaddum Object
files.description: In October 2017, an infrared sensor onboard a force protection aerostat near Al Taqaddum Air Base, Iraq, captured 17 minutes of video of an unidentified object. AARO assesses that the object was a cluster of partially and fully inflated balloons. The object's appearance is consistent with other recorded observations featuring balloon clusters. AARO employed full-motion video analysis and pixel examination techniques to inform its assessment. AARO assesses that the object did not demonstrate anomalous performance characteristics. AARO used geo-locational data from the aerostat to assess the object's speed and direction of travel.

files.title: Middle East Object
files.description: In an open hearing on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena before the Senate Armed Services Committee on April 19, Dr. Sean Kirkpatrick, director of the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO), shared a video that depicts an apparent silver, orb-like object cross the sensor’s field of view. This clip was taken by an MQ-9 in the Middle East, and while AARO assesses the object in the clip is not exhibiting anomalous behavior, the object remains unidentified. This video is a representative example of many of the cases AARO receives where there is limited data surrounding the observation. These cases are retained in AARO’s active archive pending the discovery of additional information/data that may lead to case resolution.

files.title: Middle East Red Balloon 2024
files.description: The All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office received a report from a U.S. military Service consisting of one minute and thirty-six seconds of full-motion video footage captured by a camera aboard a U.S. military platform in the Middle East in 2024. According to the reporting Service, the recording likely depicts a slow-moving spheroidal object. AARO assesses, with high confidence, that the object depicted in the video is almost certainly (≥95% likelihood) a consumer-grade reflective foil balloon. AARO bases its assessment on the object's strong morphological consistency with other resolved imagery depicting balloons and its behavioral correlation with recorded wind speed and direction during the event.

files.title: Mt. Etna Object
files.description: In December 2018, a forward-looking infrared video sensor aboard an uncrewed U.S. Air Force platform captured this footage while operating over the Mediterranean Sea. This footage depicts an object that appears to be transiting a plume of superheated gas and ash produced by an eruption of Mt. Etna, a volcano in Sicily, Italy. AARO coordinated an interagency and international analytical effort that determined that optical effects from the intense atmospheric conditions near the volcano distorted the video, causing the object to appear to transit the plume. AARO assesses with moderate confidence that the footage instead depicts a balloon approximately 170 kilometers from the caldera traveling at wind speed and direction.

files.title: NASA Audio 12/5/1965 Low Earth Orbit
files.description: This audio recording contains air to ground communications and the NASA Public Affairs audio feed with commentary, recorded during the flight of the Gemini VII mission. In this excerpted segment of audio, Astronaut Frank Borman reports to NASA mission control in Houston his sighting of an unidentified object, which he referred to as a "bogey." This sighting occurred on December 5, 1965. The dialogue includes Borman's initial report, as well as additional comments by Astronaut Jim Lovell, Borman's fellow crew member.

files.title: PR-001 Unresolved UAP Report, Africa 2022
files.description: In 2022, the United States Africa Command submitted a report of an unidentified anomalous phenomenon to the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) consisting of thirty-one seconds of video footage from an infrared sensor aboard a U.S. military platform. The footage shows an apparent heat signature with characteristics consistent with those of a physical object. However, AARO cannot determine whether the observed signature originates from a physical source, either as a thermal emission or a thermal reflection, or other source, such as a heat differential in the environment or sensor display error. The available data is insufficient to evaluate the phenomenon’s performance characteristics.

files.title: Puerto Rico Objects
files.description: On April 26, 2013, an infrared sensor onboard a U.S. Customs and Border Protection aircraft captured footage of a UAP event over the Rafael Hernandez Airport near Aguadilla, Puerto Rico. The footage appears to depict a UAP moving at high speed, splitting into two objects, and entering and exiting the water before disappearing into the ocean off Puerto Rico's northwestern coast. AARO assesses with high confidence that the objects did not demonstrate anomalous speeds or flight behaviors. An Intelligence Community partner's reconstruction of the flight path and look angle from the infrared sensor indicates that the video instead depicts two objects traveling near each other rather than a single object splitting into two. This reconstruction also demonstrates that the objects traveled in a straight line at wind speed and did not enter the water at any point.

files.title: South Asian Object 1
files.description: In an open hearing on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena before the Senate Armed Services Committee on April 19, Dr. Sean Kirkpatrick, director of the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO), shared a video depicting an unidentified object with an apparent atmospheric wake or cavitation trailing it as it moves across the sensor’s field of view from left to right. An MQ-9 forward-looking infrared video sensor captured this footage in South Asia as it was recording another MQ-9. After analysis of the full motion video, inclusion of additional footage with a longer focal length, and analysis of commercial flight data in the region, AARO assesses that the object likely is a commercial aircraft and that the trailing cavitation is a sensor artifact resultant of video compression. files.title: South Asian Object 2
files.description: In an open hearing on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena before the Senate Armed Services Committee on April 19, Dr. Sean Kirkpatrick, director of the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO), shared videos depicting an unidentified object with an apparent atmospheric wake or cavitation trailing it as it moved across the sensor’s field of view from left to right. An MQ-9 forward-looking infrared video sensor captured this footage in South Asia as it was recording another MQ-9. After analysis of the full motion video, inclusion of additional footage with a longer focal length, and analysis of commercial flight data in the region, AARO assesses that the object likely is a commercial aircraft and that the trailing cavitation is a sensor artifact resultant of video compression. Case resolution is pending final review. This video is the additional footage with a longer focal length. The apparent back and forth motion is an artifact of the longer focal length and the sensor attempting to zoom in on the fast moving UAP, rather than the MQ-9.

files.title: Western U.S. Objects
files.description: In a public meeting of NASA’s Independent Study Team on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) on May 31, 2023, Dr. Sean Kirkpatrick, director of the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO), shared a video depicting three unidentified objects recorded on infrared video in 2021 from a military range in the western United States. files.title: nasa-uap-d1-apollo-12-transcript-1969.pdf
files.description: An Apollo 12 air-to-ground voice transcript from 1969, included in the NASA UAP document release. The UAP-relevant passage is the crew discussing small "bits and pieces" floating alongside the spacecraft: on an earlier nightside pass the tracking light was seen flashing off these particles, and the commander uses their continued presence to deduce the tracking light has burned out.
files.official_note:
The transcript records crew chatter, not an investigation; the particles are discussed as ordinary spacecraft debris.
This summary is AI-generated from the document text for navigation purposes only and is not an official analysis or conclusion.

files.title: nasa-uap-d2-apollo-17-transcript-1972.pdf
files.description: An Apollo 17 air-to-ground voice transcript from 1972, included in the NASA UAP document release. The UAP-relevant passage is the crew observing a field of bright particles or fragments drifting past the spacecraft during a maneuver; they photograph them and discuss possible explanations.
files.official_note:
The transcript records crew observations and guesses, not an investigation or conclusion.
This summary is AI-generated from the document text for navigation purposes only and is not an official analysis or conclusion.

files.title: nasa-uap-d5-apollo-17-crew-debriefing-for-science-1973.pdf
files.description: A NASA "Apollo 17 Crew Debriefing for Science" transcript dated January 1973, included in the NASA UAP document release. The readable portions are scientists discussing the mission's astronomical experiments — ultraviolet astronomy, the X-ray/gamma-ray sky background, Lyman-alpha hydrogen radiation, and observations of the Coma galaxy cluster and the Earth from space.
files.official_note:
Despite its inclusion in the UAP release, the legible text does not describe an unidentified object; the connection to UAP is contextual.
This summary is AI-generated from the document text for navigation purposes only and is not an official analysis or conclusion.

files.title: serial-4-redacted_redacted.pdf
files.description: A redacted continuation page of an FBI interview record (FD-302) about a September 2023 UAP sighting. The witness describes an object that held a constant size and light intensity, first noticed while passing through a gate; the airspace had been restricted for planned drone tests, and the witness reported being shaken — sleeping poorly and having strange dreams for days afterward.
files.official_note:
Only the second page of a two-page interview continuation is present; names and most context are redacted.
This summary is AI-generated from the document text for navigation purposes only and is not an official analysis or conclusion.

files.title: serial_5_redacted_redacted.pdf
files.description: A short, redacted continuation page of an FBI interview record (FD-302) about a September 2023 UAP sighting. The only legible substantive line records that the witness thought the light might have been a meteor coming straight toward them and burning up in the atmosphere.
files.official_note:
Only a single sentence of the interview continuation is legible; all other context is redacted.
This summary is AI-generated from the document text for navigation purposes only and is not an official analysis or conclusion.

files.title: usper-statement-redacted.pdf
files.description: A redacted first-person witness statement (SECRET//NOFORN) from a senior US intelligence official who, with federal and state partners, conducted a helicopter aerial search over a mountain range after eyewitnesses reported orbs and "thuds." Over roughly two hours that night the crew repeatedly observed orbs flaring up and down in horizontal formations, swarms of lights "too many to count," objects splitting in two, and orbs that approached the helicopter and appeared to pursue nearby military aircraft.
files.official_note:
All names, units, locations and coordinates are redacted, so the site and participants cannot be identified from the document.
This summary is AI-generated from the document text for navigation purposes only and is not an official analysis or conclusion.

files.title: western_us_event_slides_5.08.2026.pdf
files.description: A federal law enforcement slide deck describing four UAP sightings in the Western U.S. by teams of special agents (USPER1–USPER7). Events include orange "mother" orbs launching smaller red orbs, a large hovering fiery orb near a rock pinnacle, and two pre-dawn "kite-shaped" objects — one dark, one apparently transparent — that moved with "zero resistance."
files.official_note:
Witness descriptions are subjective and were recorded in low-light conditions; AARO follow-up measurements differ from the agents' initial estimates.
This summary is AI-generated from the document text for navigation purposes only and is not an official analysis or conclusion.

findings.title: Source records are not proof of origin
findings.summary: The archive is best read as released government source material plus case summaries. It does not, by itself, prove extraterrestrial origin, novel propulsion, speed, altitude, or performance beyond what each source states.

findings.title: Historical records provide context, not continuity
findings.summary: The crawl includes roughly 7 historically dated groups and 56 modern groups. Historical military, FBI, NASA, and State Department records help track vocabulary and public concern, but should not be treated as evidence of one continuous phenomenon without case-level corroboration.

findings.title: The release mixes modern sensor cases with historical scans
findings.summary: The local crawl contains 70 case groups and 200 file pages. Type mix: PDF (117), Videos (61), Images (22). Agency inference from file titles and source pages is led by Department of War (102), Unknown (45), FBI (40), NASA (13).

findings.title: PURSUE is a rolling disclosure, not a finished archive
findings.summary: Release tags inferred from file/source paths: {'Release 01': 200}. The official May 22 release says a third release is being prepared, so the database is a snapshot as of 2026-05-25.

findings.title: Unresolved does not mean extraordinary
findings.summary: 11 groups carry unresolved language in the title or summary, while 10 include resolved/prosaic labels such as balloons, birds, aircraft, or optical effects. The distinction is often about available data rather than exotic characteristics.

Part 4, Stevenson talks to Bloomington, Ill., voters; rides in a motorcade through Springfield, Ill.; and poses on the porch of the Governor's mansion. Part 5 shows distance races and decathlon events at the Olympic Games, Helsinki. Ashenfelter, Zatopek, and Mathias win events.

official_records.title: Black and White Photographs of U.S. Air Force and Predecessors' Activities, Facilities, and Personnel, Domestic and Foreign
official_records.creator: Department of Defense. Department of the Air Force. 9/26/1947-
official_records.summary: The approximately 180,000 black and white negatives in this series correspond to prints in Record Group 342, Series FH ("Black and White and Color Photographs of U.S. Air Force and Predecessor Agencies Activities, Facilities and Personnel - World War II and Korean War") and Series B ("Black and White and Color Photographs of U.S. Air Force Activities, Facilities and Personnel, Domestic and Foreign"). Negatives in this series appear in two groups- some 154,000 housed in large (8 1/2"x11" or 9"x11") jackets, and some 26,000 housed in small (4 1/2"x5 1/2") jackets. The jacket size does not necessarily indicate negative size, since a majority of the negatives in the large jackets are in fact 4"x5" or smaller. A single numerical sequence spans both groups (large-jacket negatives are numbered 1 through 183007 with numerous gaps, and small-jacket negatives are numbered 155001 through 183087 with numerous gaps), with some cross-referencing for the "overlap" numbers. For those negatives numbered between 155001 and 183081 that appear in the large-jacket group, an empty jacket appears in the small-jacket group with the notation, "Original Filed in Oversize File." There are no similar cross-reference markers, however, in the large jacket group. Most of the first 5,000 items in the large-jacket group bear the agency designation "AC" (for "Air Corps," used principally on 1930's-1940's negatives but continued, for unknown reasons, into the era of the modern U.S. Air Force). Interspersed in the file are items taken earlier and bearing the "AS" (Air Service) suffix. The rest of the large jacket entries and the entirety of the small-jacket entries bear the updated "USAF" designation. Entries in both groups are, on the whole, negatives -- the original negative submitted by an Air Force photographer, an Air Force, generated copy negative, or, in some cases, both -- although there are also widely-scattered black and white transparencies and 35mm slides. Accompanying a minority of the negatives are small contact prints (placed within or attached to the respective jackets). Most of the jackets, large and small, bear information about the place, date that the image was taken, date that the image arrived at the central depository, photographic process and format, organizational source, content description, and, increasingly after the mid-1960's, photographer. The items in this series document the activities of the U.S. Air Force and its predecessors from the earliest days of military aviation through the Vietnam War. Included are combat images relating to World War I, World War II, the Korean War, post- World War II occupations of Germany and Japan, military incidents and the Cold War. Also included are photographs of aircraft, weapons, fields and installations, tests, organizations, units, and personnel. Photographs related to the history of aviation are also included.

official_records.title: Project Blue Book Case Files on Sightings of Unidentified Flying Objects (UFOs)
official_records.creator: Department of Defense. Department of the Air Force. Air Materiel Command. Intelligence Department. Technical Intelligence Division. (1947 - 1951)
official_records.summary: This series consists of the case files on sightings of unidentified flying objects (UFOs) of Project Blue Book, the U.S. Air Force (USAF) investigation into UFOs which were sighted between June 1947 and December 1969. From 1947 through 1951, the USAF Air Material Command Intelligence Department Technical Intelligence Division maintained the series. From 1951 through March 1952, the USAF Office of the Deputy Chief of Staff Operations Office of the Director of Intelligence Air Technical Intelligence Center maintained the series. From March 1952 through 1969, the USAF Air Force Systems Command Foreign Technology Division Project Blue Book Office and its predecessors maintained the series. The first subseries contains sighting case files. The second subseries contains photographs that have been withdrawn from the first subseries. The files contain the information the Air Force gathered about specific UFO sightings. Each case file relates to one sighting or to a group of closely related sightings. The files contain reports from UFO observers, correspondence between these observers and the Air Force, newspaper and magazine clippings, and reports of analyses of photographs and physical evidence. Some reports were submitted by letter or telegram, but most reports of sightings were submitted on an Air Force questionnaire which contains the name and address of the observer, date and hour of the sighting, and a description of what the observer saw. Each case file contains a control sheet which summarizes the sighting report and shows the Air Force explanation and conclusions for the sighting. There is a monthly list of sightings of unidentified flying objects for which case files were prepared. For each sighting the list contains the date, location, name of observer, and evaluation of the sighting report. The list for each month can be found at the beginning of the relevant files in this series. The case files contain cross reference sheets to photographs that can be found in the second subseries to this series. The case files also contain cross reference sheets with citations to the photographs, motion pictures, sound recordings, and artifacts that were submitted with reports and that can be found in the series "Project 'BLUE BOOK', 1954-1966" (National Archives Identifier 542184), "Project Blue Book Motion Picture Films, 1950 - 1966" (National Archives Identifier 61934), "Sound Recordings Relating to Project Blue Book Unidentified Flying Object (UFO) Investigations, 1953 - 1967" (National Archives Identifier 1142703), and "Project Bluebook Artifacts, 1952 - 1969" (National Archives Identifier 23857160).

official_records.creator: Department of Defense. Department of the Air Force. Air Force Systems Command. Foreign Technology Division. Aerial Phenomena Branch. (7/1/1961 - 12/17/1969)

From 1947 through 1951, the USAF Air Material Command Intelligence Department Technical Intelligence Division maintained the series. From 1951 through March 1952, the USAF Office of the Deputy Chief of Staff Operations Office of the Director of Intelligence Air Technical Intelligence Center maintained the series. official_records.title: Project "BLUE BOOK"
official_records.creator: Department of Defense. Department of the Air Force. Office of the Chief of Staff. Office of the Assistant Chief of Staff, Intelligence. Aerospace Technical Intelligence Center. (9/21/1959 - 7/1/1961)
official_records.summary: In December 1947, after the alleged sightings of flying saucers near Mt. Rainer, Washington, the Air Force, whose responsibilities include the air defense of the country, established Project Sign. Documentation for the project was created and acquired by the Aerial Phenomena Branch, Foreign Technology Division (FTD), Air Force Command (AFSC) until December 1969 when the UFO function was canceled by the Secretary of the Air Force. From 1951 through 1961, FTD was designated the Aerospace Technical Intelligence Center under Assistant Chief of Staff Intelligence (ASC/l), HQ USAF. Prior to that it was the Intelligence Department of Air Material Command. The purpose of Project Sign was to determine whether UFO's were a threat to the national security. In 1948 the project name was changed to Project Grudge and in 1952 the code name was again changed to Project Blue Book and the formal title to Aerial Phenomenon Group. The sightings were recorded by individuals (whose names were not released), by groups, and by the military. Film records of the alleged sightings were made in- Tulsa, Oklahoma; Australia; Fairchild AFB, Washington; Binghamton, NY; Naha, Okinawa; Snohomish, Washington; Almogordo, New Mexico; Montville, Ohio; Sandusky, Ohio; Olmsted AFB, PA; Keesler AFB, MS; Coburn, VA; and Edwards AFB, CA. There are 9 rolls of film of timed radar responses in the following locations- Wichita, Kansas; Macao, China; Edwards AFB, CA; Bermuda; Duluth, Minnesota; Queen Charlotte Islands, CANADA. There is a reference set of these records, consisting of contact sheets or positive rolled film.

official_records.title: Photographs Relating to Agency Activities, Facilities and Personnel
official_records.creator: Goddard Space Flight Center. Graphic and Publication Services Branch
official_records.summary: This series consists of photographs taken or acquired by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration's (NASA) Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC). Subjects in this series include buildings and facilities, satellite development, space telescopes, unmanned scientific spacecraft development and missions, rocket launches, manned flight missions, VIP visits, NASA personnel, and construction of the center's main campus in Greenbelt, Maryland. Photographs in this series include an image of the GSFC site plan (255-GS-1428); a view of the NASA organizational chart from August 1961 (255-GS-1230); a picture of a 1962 map of Cape Canaveral, Florida (255-GS-62-3245); and construction views of the Rosman Satellite Tracking Station in Rosman, North Carolina (255-GS-63-3208 through 255-GS-63-3231). Images of or taken by manned space missions include a launch view of Mercury-Atlas 6 (MA-6) with astronaut John Glenn on February 2, 1962 (255-GS-62-3092); in-flight photographs taken during the Gemini II (255-GS-67-2807 through 255-GS-67-2813) and Gemini VIII missions ( 255-GS-66-7086 through 255-GS-66-7094); various views from Gemini XII, including the launch, spacewalk, splashdown, and a picture of Astronauts James A. Lovell, Jr. and Buzz Aldrin posing with the spacecraft (255-GS-67-4324 through 255-GS-67-4331); and pictures relating to various Space Shuttle missions throughout the 1980s. Images relating to unmanned space missions include launch views of Mercury-Atlas 4 (MA-4) on September 13, 1961 (255-GS-62-669); pre-launch images of the Pioneer 7 space probe on August 11, 1966 (255-GS-67-4230 through 255-GS-67-4238); launch views and images of the moon taken by the Lunar Orbiter IV in May 1967 (255-GS-67-9268 through 255-GS-67-9274); and pictures taken by the Surveyor III Lander that explored the moon in April 1967 (255-GS-67-9736 through 255-GS-67-9752). Other photographs in this series include photographs relating to satellites and space telescopes, including an image of Echo I (255-GS-63-536); a launch view of the Orbiting Solar Observatory (OSO) in 1962 (255-GS-62-3096); a picture of an artist drawing of a Syncom satellite (255-GS-62-661); a view of the Intelsat II F-2 satellite being launched on January 11, 1967 (255-GS-67-4903); various mosaic images of Earth taken by Landstat satellites; and observations of Halley's Comet taken in 1985 by the International Ultraviolet Explorer (255-GS-85-5606, 255-GS-85-5607, 255-GS-85-5641 and 255-GS-85-5642). Personalities in this series include portraits of President John F. Kennedy (255-GS-1690); NASA Space Physicist Don Lind (255-GS-66-7076 to 255-GS-66-7085); Assistant Director of GSFC, E. W. Wasielewski (255-GS-328 to 255-GS-333); NASA Administrator James E. Webb (255-GS-62-391); Director of the Goddard Institute of Space Studies, Robert Jastrow (255-GS-63-1661); Chief of the GSFC Manned Space Flight Support Division, Niles R. Heller (255-GS-67-2852); Aerospace engineer and NASA project manager, Marjorie Townsend (255-GS-67-3528); National Space Science Data Center (NSSDC) Director James Vette (255-GS-67-4742); Marshall Space Flight Center Director Wernher von Braun (255-GS-67-8545); and a reproduction of a group portrait of the Mercury Seven astronauts (255-GS-2026). Also included are views of Apollo Mission Director William Schneider visiting GSFC in September 1967 (255-GS-68-637 and 255-GS-68-638); astronauts Gus Grissom and Deke Slayton visiting GSFC in March 1961; astronaut John Glenn and broadcast journalist Walter Cronkite visiting GSFC in March 1965 (255-GS-65-7068); Manned Flight Support Director Ozro M. Covington at his desk in November 1966 (255-GS-67-3501); and astronaut John Glenn visiting Pope Paul VI in October 1965 during the first NASA goodwill tour of Europe (255-GS-66-4472). In addition, this series includes pictures of VIP visits to the center's main campus including Robert H. Goddard on September 27. 1961 (255-GS-62-482 through 255-GS-62-491); President John F. Kennedy on July 8, 1962 (255-GS-63-124); Vice President Hubert H. Humphrey on March 14, 1966 (255-GS-66-5436); and President Richard M. Nixon visiting during the Apollo 13 mission (255-GS-70-7539 to 255-GS-70-7566).

official_records.summary: This series documents the sighting of an unidentified flying object (UFO) by the crew of Japan Airlines flight 1628 while in Alaskan air space. There are transcripts of the pilot's communication with air traffic control personnel; a text of an interview with the captain, Federal Aviation Administration personnel, and an interpreter as well as with the flight engineer and co-pilot. There are also diagrams drawn by the captain detailing the position of the UFO relative to his airplane during the sighting, and a copy of his personal statement on the event. osint_methods.title: Check normal airspace activity
osint_methods.summary: Correlate time and location against aircraft, ADS-B tracks, military training areas, NOTAMs, launch windows, rocket reentries, drones, balloons, and weather data.
osint_methods.tools: ADS-B Exchange, FlightRadar24 history, FAA data, NOTAMs, Space-Track, weather archives

osint_methods.title: Check astronomy and satellites
osint_methods.summary: Many reports need comparison with planets, meteors, satellite flares, Starlink trains, reentries, and local sky geometry before stronger claims are entertained.
osint_methods.tools: Stellarium, Heavens-Above, CelesTrak, Space-Track, meteor shower calendars

osint_methods.title: Preserve chain of custody
osint_methods.summary: Track where a file came from, whether it is an official asset, a mirror, an uploaded derivative, or a social-media repost. Treat metadata loss and re-encoding as evidence-quality changes.
osint_methods.tools: source URLs, hashes, archive snapshots, original download pages

osint_methods.title: Model parallax, focus, and optical artifacts
osint_methods.summary: Small nearby objects, camera stabilization, glare, bokeh, thermal blooming, and platform motion can mimic high speed or unusual maneuvers in 2D footage.
osint_methods.tools: frame stepping, camera geometry, lens specs, background motion, independent landmarks

osint_methods.title: Run a recursive research loop
osint_methods.summary: Every new item should cycle through collect, normalize, correlate, challenge, and queue. The loop keeps integrating new releases while preserving uncertainty and provenance.
osint_methods.tools: source manifests, metadata templates, baseline comparisons, confidence scoring, next-action queue

osint_methods.title: Separate report volume from event volume
osint_methods.summary: Crowdsourced sighting spikes can reflect media attention, internet access, reporting behavior, and database collection practices rather than changes in phenomena.
osint_methods.tools: date normalization, population controls, media event timelines, duplicate detection

osint_methods.title: Document sensor and platform context
osint_methods.summary: For video or imagery, record camera type, field of view, platform motion, frame rate, compression, overlays, timestamp, pointing angle, and any missing telemetry before estimating object behavior.
osint_methods.tools: DVIDS/AARO descriptions, video overlays, EXIF/metadata, frame extraction

osint_methods.title: Integrate by evidence class
osint_methods.summary: Official records, public reports, scientific baselines, OSINT analyses, and claims should stay separable but cross-queryable. Integration should reveal overlap without flattening reliability.
osint_methods.tools: entity extraction, source reliability bands, temporal/geographic joins, alternative-hypothesis baselines

osint_methods.title: Compare prosaic morphology
osint_methods.summary: Resolved cases often turn on morphology, wind correlation, wings/balloon movement, thermal signature, or motion consistent with birds, balloons, aircraft, or airborne debris.
osint_methods.tools: wind profiles, NOAA weather, visual comparison libraries, AARO resolved-case reports

research_signals.title: Natural and human-made baseline layers are now queryable
research_signals.summary: NASA CNEOS contributes 876 geocoded fireball/bolide records through 2026-05-21 02:15:51, while FAA quarterly files contribute 11647 UAS/drone reports through 2025-12-30. These baselines help challenge bright-light and low-altitude reports.
research_signals.next_step: Add time-window joins when a case has precise timestamp and location metadata.

research_signals.title: Coverage gaps are tracked instead of hidden
research_signals.summary: 40 official source leads currently have collection-level provenance but no row-level harvested records in the local database. That is expected for portals without bulk APIs, multilingual catalogs, or account-gated archives.
research_signals.next_step: Convert the highest-value official portals into parsers only when the source offers stable public search pages, files, or APIs.

research_signals.title: Global government coverage is now explicit
research_signals.summary: The source catalog covers 22 official or reported-official jurisdictions: African Union, Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, China, Denmark, European Union, France, Germany, India, International, Japan.... Provenance bands: {'official_primary': 10, 'official_report': 22, 'scientific_context': 17, 'official_archive': 145, 'crowdsourced': 2, 'public_index': 4}.
research_signals.next_step: Prioritize jurisdictions with official case databases or digitized archives before adding weaker press-only sources.

research_signals.title: Recursive research loop is database-backed
research_signals.summary: The current snapshot can run collect-normalize-correlate-challenge-queue across 70 case groups, 200 released files, 111 official catalog records, 80332 public sightings, and 12523 baseline events.
research_signals.next_step: Use the Intel view to treat every finding as a living research lead with a next action, not as a final claim.

research_signals.title: Source health is strong enough for a command-center view
research_signals.summary: The atlas now separates 189 official, official-international, or reported-official source collections from public indexes, scientific projects, and crowdsourced datasets, so mixed-source exploration can preserve reliability bands.
research_signals.next_step: Keep every new source assigned to a reliability band before it is mixed into search, maps, or findings.

research_signals.title: Highly connected cases deserve priority review
research_signals.summary: 66 case groups have at least four generated cross-reference edges. These are good starting points for manual comparison because they share dates, agencies, locations, release tranches, or vocabulary with multiple records.
research_signals.next_step: Inspect the top connected cases side by side and separate meaningful overlaps from generic shared terms.

research_signals.title: Modern release watch should stay active
research_signals.summary: 24 crawled file records contain 2024-2026 incident-date signals or release context. PURSUE is a rolling archive, so new tranches can change cluster weights and source coverage.
research_signals.next_step: Rebuild the database after new WAR.GOV/PURSUE tranches and compare counts against the previous static snapshot.

research_signals.title: Official metadata is still uneven
research_signals.summary: National Archives and AARO records are rolling and not uniformly structured. Some bulk metadata files can be malformed or too large to parse cleanly, so the atlas keeps source links even when row-level metadata cannot be ingested.
research_signals.next_step: Track skipped or malformed official exports as a source-health issue rather than silently dropping them from the audit trail.

research_signals.title: Public report volume is useful but bias-heavy
research_signals.summary: The public report dataset is dominated by light shape reports (16565) and US country reports (65114), which is a reporting pattern as much as an event pattern.
research_signals.next_step: Normalize future density maps by population, internet access, and media-attention periods before drawing strong geographic conclusions.
